title: Which Snowflake ETL tool fits you?

questions.hint: This matters most. Snowflake's own loading only helps once something has produced files or rows.

options.label: Files or rows my own apps already produce
options.why: Snowpipe loads files and rows without another vendor

options.label: Many SaaS apps
options.why: these tools run the SaaS connectors for you

options.label: A live database with ongoing changes
Older sources like Db2, Oracle or SAP
options.why: you need a wide source list

options.label: It is already in Snowflake and needs reshaping
options.why: the data is already loaded, so you need SQL transforms inside Snowflake

options.label: Snowflake runs it
options.why: you want one vendor and one contract

options.label: We run open source on our own servers
options.why: you want self-hosted open source, and Airbyte Core and OLake Go are the ones the post covers

questions.q: How fresh does the data need to be?
questions.hint: Faster syncs keep a warehouse awake, so freshness adds Snowflake credits.

options.label: Hourly is fine
options.why: hourly syncs are the cheapest on the Snowflake side

options.label: Within a few minutes
options.why: Snowpipe loads within minutes after files arrive

options.label: Seconds, close to live
options.why: Snowpipe Streaming and Estuary aim at low latency

questions.q: What does your budget look like?

options.label: I want a free way to start
options.why: these have a free plan, free Core or a trial

options.label: I need a published price to plan from
Large budget, a contract is fine
options.why: these are sold by quote, in large bundles or at higher plan tiers

questions.q: Do you need Iceberg tables that Snowflake reads?
questions.hint: Several of these options are Beta or Early Access, so check early.

options.label: Yes
options.why: these document some Iceberg path, though some are Beta or Early Access

snowpipe.name: Snowflake loading (Snowpipe)
snowpipe.summary: Snowflake's own ways in: COPY INTO, Snowpipe, Snowpipe Streaming and a Kafka connector.
snowpipe.bestWhen: your apps or an upstream tool already produce files in cloud storage or rows in a stream.
snowpipe.watchOut: these load data but do not read your databases or SaaS apps, so something else must produce the files or rows.

openflow.name: Snowflake Openflow
openflow.summary: A Snowflake-run connector service built on Apache NiFi, billed per vCPU-hour.
openflow.bestWhen: you already pay Snowflake and want database change capture from one vendor.
openflow.watchOut: most Openflow connectors bring data into Snowflake, and change capture connectors need a Snowflake warehouse.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A managed service billed on monthly active rows, counted per connection.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want a vendor to own connector upkeep for many SaaS apps and databases.
fivetran.watchOut: the meter counts changed rows, and Lakehouse tables are Beta.

hevo.name: Hevo
hevo.summary: A managed tool billed on events, with a free plan.
hevo.bestWhen: you are a small team with common sources and want a free start.
hevo.watchOut: updated records count as billable events, so busy tables cost more, and its Snowflake Iceberg destination is Early Access.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A large open-source connector library, free to self-host as Core, with a paid cloud.
airbyte.bestWhen: you have engineers and want the widest open-source connector set.
airbyte.watchOut: its docs say CDC runs as scheduled syncs, and self-hosting moves the bill to servers and staff.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: A managed streaming service billed by gigabytes plus connector instances.
estuary.bestWhen: you need low-latency change capture into Snowflake.
estuary.watchOut: each connector instance adds $50 to $100 a month, and its licence is not open source (checked Oct 2026).

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Open-source replication that creates Iceberg tables in a Snowflake database through the Snowflake Horizon Catalog, from v0.11.0.
olake.bestWhen: your sources are databases, Kafka topics or S3 files, you want open-source software on your own servers, and you want Iceberg tables in a Snowflake database.
olake.watchOut: it runs on your own servers, and Snowflake Horizon Catalog support starts at v0.11.0.

matillion.name: Matillion
matillion.summary: A visual designer whose transformations run as SQL inside your Snowflake warehouse.
matillion.bestWhen: your team likes a visual designer and most of the work is transformation in Snowflake.
matillion.watchOut: the price is not published, so you need a quote.

informatica.name: Informatica
informatica.summary: An enterprise suite with a wide source list, billed in processing units.
informatica.bestWhen: you are a large company with older sources like Db2 and Oracle and want one vendor contract.
informatica.watchOut: its public pages show no price per processing unit, so you cannot plan a budget from them alone.

dbt.name: dbt or Snowflake dynamic tables
dbt.summary: SQL transforms that run after a loader has put the data in Snowflake.
dbt.bestWhen: your raw data is already in Snowflake and your team writes SQL.
dbt.watchOut: neither one moves data into Snowflake, and both add Snowflake compute cost.
